disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Minnesota DNR before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.general: Residents and nonresidents 16 and over need a small game license AND a trapping license to take furbearers with traps. Residents under 13 need no trapping license; ages 13-17 need a junior trapping license. Persons born after December 31, 1989 need a trapper education certificate (or apprentice trapper validation) to obtain a trapping license. Nonresidents may trap only on land they own in Minnesota. A person may not take pine marten, fisher, mink, muskrat, beaver, or otter by firearms or archery hunting (a firearm may be used to dispatch an animal already taken in a trap).
license_summary.trapping_hours: Trapping hours are 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. Traps may not be set or tended for fox, badger, opossum, mink, muskrat, beaver, otter, or raccoon before 9 a.m. on opening day.

species.iac_reference: Minnesota Rules 6234; 2026 MN Hunting Regulations pp.65-66
species.notes: 2026 change: trappers present only the HEADS of bobcats at furbearer registration (full carcasses no longer required). Keep male and female heads separated for placement in bins.
permit_requirements: Season bag limit: 5 bobcats combined (hunting + trapping), with no more than 1 bobcat from south of I-94.

Pelts, heads, and completed site-validated trapping coupons (electronic or paper) must be presented for registration at a DNR registration station or area wildlife office before the pelt is sold or removed from the state, and no more than 48 hours after the season closes.
Fisher, otter, bobcat, or pine marten taken by a resident under age 5 must be included in the limit of the accompanying parent or guardian.

verification.confirmation_notes: Data taken from the official 2026 Minnesota Hunting Regulations (mndnr.gov PDF, downloaded 2026-09-18, archived locally). Furbearer hunting seasons table and trapping seasons table (pp.65-66); furbearer zone boundary ('North Furbearer Zone is north of the Interstate 94 / Hwy 10 line'); 2026 furbearer registration requirements (bobcat heads-only rule, 48-hour post-close registration for fisher/pine marten/bobcat, otter registration through May 17, 2027); no-open-season mammal list (lynx, wolverine, cougar, wolf, spotted skunk). Trapping hours 5 a.m.-10 p.m. with a 9 a.m. opening-day restriction for listed species.
known_gaps: Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in the Minnesota guide.

Coyote and striped skunk are listed as continuous under HUNTING (unprotected animals). Their trapping seasons were not stated in the extracted guide sections; only hunting seasons were modeled — verify against Minnesota Rules 6234 for trapping.

The 48-hour post-close registration deadlines for fisher/pine marten/bobcat are: register before the pelt is sold or removed from the state AND no more than 48 hours after the season closes (with appointment option for unavoidable conflicts).
Season close dates that fall after the current compilation date but in the same season year (e.g., beaver through May 15, 2027) are as published.
